# ztd charts

> ztd charts (npm package ztd-charts) is a React 18+ chart library with 44 animated, interactive, accessible chart types drawn in pure SVG. It has zero runtime dependencies: react and react-dom are peer dependencies. Each chart can be written as a JSON spec { type, data, encoding, options, card } and rendered with <Chart spec/>, validated against a JSON Schema, drawn to PNG, SVG or HTML by the ztd-charts CLI, or picked and drawn by AI agents through a stdio MCP server. MIT license.

Key facts:

- Language: English by default. Locale "ko-KR" (a chart's locale prop, options.locale in a spec, or <ThemeProvider locale="ko-KR">) switches number formats (1.2만, 3.4억, ₩5,000) and the text charts write themselves (tooltips, screen reader sentences, badges) to Korean.
- Theme: dark by default (ink cards, lime accent). theme="light" gives white cards with a sky-blue accent. Every color is a --ztd-* CSS variable.
- Design: one highlighted item in the accent color, everything else neutral. <ChartCard> adds a number, a bold title, a gray subtitle, a small square legend, a one-line takeaway and a level badge (Basic, Intermediate, Advanced; 기본, 중급, 심화 in Korean).
- Accessibility: keyboard navigation (Tab, arrow keys, Enter), a screen reader description and a hidden data table on every chart, and the reduced motion setting.

Install:

- Library: `npm i ztd-charts` (React 18 or later)
- CLI: `npx ztd-charts-cli <command>`. Commands: list, info, schema, example, validate, render, init, suggest. Installed, the command is `ztd-charts`. Never run `npx ztd-charts`: that is the chart library, which has no command. Add `--locale ko` for Korean output.
- MCP server in Claude Code: `claude mcp add ztd-charts -- npx -y ztd-charts-mcp`
- MCP server in a JSON config (Claude Desktop, Cursor): `{ "mcpServers": { "ztd-charts": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "ztd-charts-mcp"] } } }`. Tools: list_charts, get_chart_schema, validate_spec, render_chart, suggest_chart.
- Agent skill: copy skills/ztd-charts/ from the repository to .claude/skills/ztd-charts/ (Claude Code) or .cursor/skills/ztd-charts/ (Cursor).

Usage:

```tsx
import { Chart, ChartCard, PieChart } from "ztd-charts";

const data = [{"device":"Mobile","sales":72},{"device":"Desktop","sales":23},{"device":"Tablet","sales":5}];

// A component. Encoding channels are props with the same name
<ChartCard number="01" title="Pie chart" subtitle="Sales share by device" takeaway="Only 2 to 4 items" level="basic">
  <PieChart data={data} label="device" value="sales" highlight="Mobile" />
</ChartCard>

// The same chart from a JSON spec, card included
<Chart spec={{"type":"pie","data":[{"device":"Mobile","sales":72},{"device":"Desktop","sales":23},{"device":"Tablet","sales":5}],"encoding":{"label":"device","value":"sales"},"options":{"highlight":"Mobile"},"card":{"number":"01","title":"Pie chart","subtitle":"Sales share by device","takeaway":"Only 2 to 4 items","level":"basic","legend":"auto"}}} />
```

Channels whose prop name differs: gauge value -> valueKey, gauge target -> targetKey.

Entry points:

- `ztd-charts`: the 44 chart components (<PieChart>, <LineChart> and so on), <Chart spec/>, <ChartCard>, <ChartGrid>, <ChartFacets> (small multiples), <ChartState>, <ThemeProvider>, useChartData, number formatters
- `ztd-charts/spec`: works without React. CHARTS (the registry), validateSpec, specSchema, schemaFor, suggestCharts, chartsIn, localizeDef, sample data
- `ztd-charts/server`: renderSpecToSVG (a standalone SVG with the card frame), renderSpecToHTML, resolveSpecData
- `ztd-charts/schema.json`: JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for every spec. One chart: `ztd-charts/schema/charts/<type>.schema.json`

Spec:

- type: one of the 44 types below. Aliases: doughnut -> donut, column -> bar, stackedBar -> bar, groupedBar -> bar, stacked -> area, streamgraph -> stream, radial -> radialBar, radialbar -> radialBar, progress -> gauge, progressRing -> gauge, kpi -> gauge, violin -> box, boxplot -> box, calendarHeatmap -> calendar, parallel-coordinates -> parallel, parallelCoordinates -> parallel, mekko -> marimekko, spider -> radar, ohlc -> candlestick, candle -> candlestick, stock -> candlestick, segment -> segmented, segmentedBar -> segmented, proportionBar -> segmented, stackedBar100 -> segmented, hist -> histogram, tilemap -> tileMap, tileGrid -> tileMap, cartogram -> tileMap, barChartRace -> barRace, racingBar -> barRace, racingBars -> barRace, raceBar -> barRace, arcDiagram -> network, graph -> network, nodeLink -> network, gantt -> timeline, ganttChart -> timeline, schedule -> timeline, dendrogram -> tree, orgChart -> tree, treeChart -> tree, choroplethMap -> choropleth, filledMap -> choropleth, map -> choropleth, bubbleMap -> symbolMap, proportionalSymbolMap -> symbolMap, pointMap -> symbolMap, originDestination -> flowMap, odMap -> flowMap
- data: an array of row objects, { values }, { csv } or { url, format?, select? }. <Chart>, the CLI and the MCP render_chart tool fetch the url.
- encoding: channel -> field name. y can be an array of fields for wide tables.
- options.highlight: Item to highlight. An index, a name, an array, or "max" | "min" | "first" | "last" | "none". Without it, each chart picks its own default (listed per chart in llms-full.txt).
- options.format: Value format. "number" | "integer" | "percent" (values are already percents: 42 → "42%") | "ratio" (0.42 → "42%") | "compact" | "currency" (KRW for Korean locales, otherwise USD; for another currency pass Intl options with currency) | "decimal" or Intl.NumberFormat options. options.unit is text appended to each value.
- Other common options: height, width, locale, animate, duration, easing (spring|easeOut|easeInOut|linear), stagger, reducedMotion, animateOnView, showLabels, tooltip, syncId, ariaLabel, description. Each chart adds its own options.
- card: { number, title, subtitle, takeaway, level: "basic" | "intermediate" | "advanced" (Korean "기본" | "중급" | "심화" also accepted), legend: "auto" | "toggle" | [{ label, color }], sample, source, note, accent, download: true | ["csv", "svg", "png"] }
- facet: { by, columns?, scale?: "shared" | "free" } (line, area, bar, scatter only). Small multiples: the same chart once per value of one field, in a grid, with hover shared across panels. For when one chart would hold too many series to read. by: Field to split by, for example "region". One panel per value in first-appearance order, up to 24 (more than 24 values: the first 24 are drawn and validateSpec warns). columns: Most panels per row. Without it, as many as fit at a panel width of 140px or more. scale: "shared" (default) puts every panel on one value scale (and one date or number x range) so heights compare. "free" fits each panel to its own data and labels every value axis. options.highlight set to a by value draws that panel in the accent color and the rest in neutral; any other highlight goes to every panel. Each panel is a full accessible chart named "<card title>, <value>". The CLI render command and the MCP render_chart tool draw it as one image. React without a spec: <ChartFacets chart={LineChart} type="line" data={rows} by="region" chartProps={{ x: "week", y: "orders" }} />
- JSON Schema: https://unpkg.com/ztd-charts/schema/chart-spec.schema.json
- Korean: from ztd-charts/spec, chartsIn("ko") and localizeDef(def, "ko") return Korean names, descriptions and example specs; specSchemaIn("ko") and schemaForIn(type, "ko") return the JSON Schema with Korean descriptions (specSchema() and schemaFor(type) are English); validateSpec(spec, { lang: "ko" }) and suggestCharts(rows, { lang: "ko" }) return Korean messages; GROUPS and LEVELS hold both labels

Data helpers:

- useChartData(url | async fn, { select, parse, refreshMs, init }) -> { data, loading, error, empty, reload }
- parseCSV, fromRows (2D arrays, SQL rows + columns, Sheets values), fromObjects (key-value maps, column maps), melt, normalizeData
- percentile(values, 95) and percentiles(rows, { by, value, p: [50, 95, 99] }) -> rows with p50, p95, p99 per group, for p95 latency charts. BoxPlot whiskers: [5, 95] sets whisker ends to percentiles.
- Accessors accept a field name (dot paths ok) or a function (d, i) => value. Strings like "1,234", "12%", "₩5,000" are read as numbers.
- <ChartState loading error empty onRetry> shows matching states at chart height.

Charts (type, component, English name, Korean name, level):

- pie (<PieChart>, Pie chart, 파이 차트, basic): Each item's share of the whole. encoding: label, value. use: 2 to 4 items that add up to 100%. avoid: More than 4 items, or values close to each other (bars are more accurate).
- donut (<DonutChart>, Donut chart, 도넛 차트, basic): A share chart with the total in the center. encoding: label, value. use: The total matters as much as the shares. avoid: More than 6 items.
- funnel (<FunnelChart>, Funnel chart, 퍼널 차트, basic): How much drops at each stage, with conversion rates. encoding: label, value. use: Ordered steps such as a sign-up or purchase flow. avoid: The steps have no order, or values grow from step to step.
- waffle (<WaffleChart>, Waffle chart, 와플 차트, intermediate): Proportion on a 100-cell grid, or one dot per unit in a half circle (seat chart). encoding: label, value. use: A share reads better as a count, like '38 out of 100', or seats out of a fixed total. avoid: More than 4 items, or differences under 1% matter.
- treemap (<Treemap>, Treemap, 트리맵, intermediate): Shares of a hierarchy shown as area. encoding: label, value, group?. use: Two levels of share at once, such as products within categories. avoid: Exact size comparison matters.
- sunburst (<SunburstChart>, Sunburst, 선버스트, intermediate): A hierarchy drawn in rings. encoding: label, value, group?. use: A breakdown of 2 to 3 levels, such as channel > campaign. avoid: 4 or more levels, or more than 20 leaves.
- waterfall (<WaterfallChart>, Waterfall chart, 폭포 차트, intermediate): Breaks the change from a start value to an end value into its drivers. encoding: label, value, type?. use: Explaining why last month's revenue became this month's. avoid: More than 12 drivers.
- pareto (<ParetoChart>, Pareto chart, 파레토 차트, intermediate): Bars sorted largest first with a cumulative share line. encoding: label, value. use: Seeing how few items make up 80% of the total. avoid: The item order means something (time order, for example).
- marimekko (<MarimekkoChart>, Marimekko chart, 마리메코 차트, advanced): Two shares at once: width (column share) and height (share within the column). encoding: x, series, value. use: Revenue size by channel and device mix in one chart. avoid: More than 6 columns or more than 4 series.
- heatmap (<Heatmap>, Heatmap, 히트맵, intermediate): Values where two categories meet, shown as color depth. encoding: x, y, value. use: Finding patterns such as orders by weekday × hour. avoid: Exact value comparison matters.
- radar (<RadarChart>, Radar chart, 레이더 차트, intermediate): Compares several metrics at once. encoding: axis, value[], series?. use: Products or candidates scored on 5 to 8 metrics. avoid: More than 3 series (they overlap and get hard to read).
- bubble (<BubbleChart>, Bubble chart, 버블 차트, intermediate): Three values at once: x, y and size. Without size it is a scatter plot. encoding: x, y, size?, label?. use: How three metrics relate, such as CPC, ROAS and spend by campaign. avoid: Dots overlap and sizes get hard to compare.
- line (<LineChart>, Line chart, 라인 차트, basic): Change over time. encoding: x, y[], series?, lower?[], upper?[]. use: A metric over time, such as monthly users, alone or against other series. avoid: x is a category with no order.
- area (<AreaChart>, Area chart, 영역 차트, basic): Running totals and a changing mix (stacked, 100% stacked). encoding: x, y[], series?, lower?[], upper?[]. use: Seeing how each channel's traffic changes within the total. avoid: The exact value of each series matters.
- stream (<StreamGraph>, Streamgraph, 스트림그래프, advanced): Many series as flowing bands that show size and change. encoding: x, y[], series?. use: 5 or more series where the rhythm of the flow matters, such as viewing by genre. avoid: You need to read exact values.
- bar (<BarChart>, Bar chart, 막대 차트, basic): Grouped, stacked, 100%, diverging and horizontal bars, with optional lines on the same axis. encoding: x, y[], series?, line?[]. use: Comparing sizes across categories precisely. avoid: The flow over time is the point (a line works better).
- radialBar (<RadialBarChart>, Radial bar chart, 방사형 막대, intermediate): Ratios such as progress toward goals, drawn as rings. encoding: label, value. use: Showing progress on 3 to 6 goals in one view. avoid: Comparing values precisely (outer rings look longer).
- gauge (<GaugeChart>, Gauge, 게이지, basic): One KPI's current value against its target. encoding: value, target?. use: Showing one value against its target, large. avoid: Comparing several values.
- bullet (<BulletChart>, Bullet chart, 불릿 차트, intermediate): Actual value against a target and bands (poor, fair, good). encoding: label, value, target?. use: Several KPIs with their targets in a small space. avoid: There is no target or band.
- sparkline (<Sparkline>, Sparkline, 스파크라인, basic): A small trend line next to a table cell or KPI. encoding: x?, y. use: The trend matters more than exact values. avoid: You need to read axis values.
- slope (<SlopeChart>, Slope chart, 슬로프 차트, intermediate): Change in size and rank between two points in time. encoding: label, x?, value?. use: Comparing just two points in time, such as last year's and this year's share. avoid: 3 or more points in time (use a line or bump chart).
- dumbbell (<DumbbellChart>, Dumbbell chart, 덤벨 차트, intermediate): The gap between two values per item (before and after, target and actual). encoding: label, start, end. use: The gap is the story, such as before and after an improvement by region. avoid: There is only one value.
- lollipop (<LollipopChart>, Lollipop chart, 롤리팝 차트, basic): A line and a dot instead of a bar. Stays light with many items. encoding: label, value. use: Rankings of 7 to 20 items, such as usage by feature. avoid: The differences between values are very small.
- beeswarm (<BeeswarmChart>, Beeswarm, 비스웜, advanced): A distribution with every dot laid out without overlap. encoding: value, group?, label?. use: Seeing each user's value, group by group. avoid: Thousands of dots that overlap (use violin or ridgeline).
- ridgeline (<RidgelineChart>, Ridgeline, 릿지라인, advanced): Group distributions as overlapping, stacked curves. encoding: group, value. use: Comparing distributions across 5 to 12 groups, such as delivery time by region. avoid: 3 or fewer groups (a box plot is simpler).
- sankey (<SankeyChart>, Sankey diagram, 생키 다이어그램, advanced): How much flows between stages. encoding: source, target, value. use: User flow from traffic source to purchase or drop-off. avoid: The flow loops back, or there are more than 30 nodes.
- chord (<ChordChart>, Chord diagram, 코드 다이어그램, advanced): How much groups send to and receive from each other. encoding: source, target, value. use: Two-way relationships, such as requests between teams. avoid: More than 10 groups.
- calendar (<CalendarHeatmap>, Calendar heatmap, 캘린더 히트맵, intermediate): Daily amounts on a weekly grid. encoding: date, value. use: The rhythm of daily activity, such as commits or orders. avoid: The period is shorter than a month.
- bump (<BumpChart>, Bump chart, 범프 차트, intermediate): Rank changes over time. encoding: x, series, rank?, value?. use: What matters is the rank, as in App Store rankings. avoid: The value gaps between ranks matter.
- box (<BoxPlot>, Box / violin plot, 박스 플롯, advanced): Distribution summary by group (quartiles, median, outliers). encoding: group, value. use: Distribution and outliers together, such as response time by API. avoid: The audience is not used to quartiles (a beeswarm is easier).
- parallel (<ParallelCoordinates>, Parallel coordinates, 평행 좌표, advanced): Several numeric metrics, each on its own axis, compared as one line per row. encoding: label?. use: Comparing 4 to 8 metrics at once, such as product specs. avoid: The audience sees it for the first time (it needs explaining).
- candlestick (<CandlestickChart>, Candlestick chart, 캔들스틱, advanced): Open, high, low and close for each period in one candle. encoding: x, open, high, low, close, volume?. use: Stocks, exchange rates or coins, where the swing within each period matters. avoid: A trend with only one value (a line chart is cleaner).
- segmented (<SegmentedBar>, Segmented bar, 비율 막대, basic): One whole split into a bar by share, with a list. encoding: label, value. use: Showing the mix in one line inside a card (2 to 6 items). avoid: Comparing similar values, or many items (a bar chart is more accurate).
- skyline (<SkylineChart>, Skyline, 스카이라인, intermediate): Stacked volume per period as blocks, with a smaller outcome in the same unit standing in front. encoding: x, y[], series?, front?[]. use: 7 to 40 periods of stacked volume and a smaller outcome in the same unit (failures, retries), as the lead card of a dashboard. avoid: Negative values, precise value comparison (bars are more accurate), or two values in different units (split the chart and link it with syncId).
- histogram (<HistogramChart>, Histogram, 히스토그램, intermediate): Distribution of raw samples with its tail and the share past a limit. encoding: value?, group?, x0?, x1?, count?. use: 30 or more raw samples, such as request latency, where the tail and the share past a limit matter. avoid: Comparing categories (use bars), or fewer than 10 samples (a beeswarm fits better).
- scatter (<ScatterChart>, Scatter plot, 산점도, basic): How two numbers relate, one dot per item, colored by series. encoding: x, y, series?, label?. use: How two numeric values relate, such as cost and latency per request, with up to 4 series. avoid: x is time (a line works better), or there are more than 50,000 dots without bin "hex".
- tileMap (<TileMap>, Tile grid map, 타일 격자 지도, intermediate): One equal tile per region, placed roughly where it is and shaded by its value. encoding: region, value. use: Comparing one value across the regions of a country, such as a rate per state, where small regions matter as much as large ones. avoid: Exact borders, distances or areas matter, or the regions are not in a built-in grid and you have no layout for them.
- choropleth (<Choropleth>, Choropleth map, 단계구분도, intermediate): Regions on a real map, shaded by their value in steps. encoding: region, value. use: Where is it high and where is it low: a rate or average per country, state or province, where the geographic pattern is the message. avoid: The values are totals that grow with area or population (large regions look heavier), or every region must be equally visible (use tileMap).
- barRace (<BarRace>, Bar race, 막대 레이스, intermediate): Horizontal bars ranked at each time step that move to their new length and place as the steps play. encoding: label, value, frame. use: Telling how a ranking changed over time in a talk or a video, such as sales by brand per year. avoid: Readers need to compare exact values or ranks across time (a bump chart or a line chart does that better), or there is only one time step.
- network (<NetworkChart>, Network, 네트워크, advanced): Who is connected to whom, and who sits at the center. encoding: source, target, value?. use: The structure of links matters more than their amount, such as calls between services, collaboration between teams or links between documents. avoid: The amount moving between stages is the point (sankey, chord), the links form a tree (sunburst), or there are more than about 300 nodes.
- timeline (<Timeline>, Timeline, 타임라인, intermediate): When things started and ended, and what overlapped: one bar per item on a time axis. encoding: label, start, end, group?, status?. use: Items with a start and an end, such as a project schedule, deployment and job runs, an agent run log or an incident timeline. avoid: Each item has one value and no start or end (use bar), or the dependencies between tasks are the story.
- tree (<Tree>, Tree, 트리, intermediate): The parent and child links of a hierarchy, drawn as dots joined by curves. encoding: label, value?, group?, id?, parent?. use: The structure itself is the point: an org chart, a folder or dependency tree, what an outage reaches, a decision tree. avoid: Each part's share of the total matters more than the links (treemap or sunburst), or the leaves are thousands of items to compare by size.
- symbolMap (<SymbolMap>, Symbol map, 기호 지도, intermediate): One circle per place on a pale map, its area proportional to the value. encoding: lon?, lat?, size?, label?, region?, group?. use: Amounts that sit at a point, such as users per city, revenue per store or traffic per data centre, where absolute sizes should compare directly. avoid: The value is a rate across a whole region (use choropleth), or the places are so many and so close that circles cover each other (aggregate first).
- flowMap (<FlowMap>, Flow map, 흐름 지도, advanced): Curved links between places on a map, their width proportional to the amount. encoding: source, target, value?. use: From where to where and how much: shipments, migration, transfers or traffic between regions, where direction and distance matter. avoid: Only the amounts matter and places have no meaningful position (use sankey or chord), or there are hundreds of crossing flows.

Bundle size per chart (Brotli by size-limit, one import including the shared core, React excluded): PieChart 13.88 KB, DonutChart 13.9 KB, FunnelChart 12.3 KB, WaffleChart 15.11 KB, Treemap 12.83 KB, SunburstChart 13.21 KB, WaterfallChart 13.47 KB, ParetoChart 13.75 KB, MarimekkoChart 13.13 KB, Heatmap 14.24 KB, RadarChart 13.72 KB, BubbleChart 16.66 KB, LineChart 26.2 KB, AreaChart 26.2 KB, StreamGraph 16.47 KB, BarChart 21.9 KB, RadialBarChart 11.88 KB, GaugeChart 12.03 KB, BulletChart 12.68 KB, Sparkline 14.55 KB, SlopeChart 12.77 KB, DumbbellChart 12.28 KB, LollipopChart 13.11 KB, BeeswarmChart 14.07 KB, RidgelineChart 12.96 KB, SankeyChart 13.54 KB, ChordChart 12.54 KB, CalendarHeatmap 15.1 KB, BumpChart 14.49 KB, BoxPlot 14.36 KB, ParallelCoordinates 13.64 KB, CandlestickChart 20.18 KB, SegmentedBar 12.48 KB, SkylineChart 18.65 KB, HistogramChart 18.35 KB, ScatterChart 22.49 KB, TileMap 15.84 KB, Choropleth 19.05 KB, SymbolMap 20.28 KB, FlowMap 20.96 KB, Tree 16.94 KB, Timeline 19.93 KB, BarRace 17.66 KB, NetworkChart 15.87 KB, StatCard 15.17 KB, LiveLineChart 13.62 KB
